    10→_NAME_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9-]+$")
    11→
    12→
    13→def _validate_name(name: str) -> None:
    14→    if not name or len(name) > 64 or not _NAME_PATTERN.match(name):
    15→        raise SkillValidationError(
    16→            "Skill name must be 1-64 characters, lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens."
    17→        )
    18→
    19→
    20→def _parse_skill_md(text: str) -> dict:
    21→    """Parse a SKILL.md file into {name, description, content}."""
    22→    if not text.startswith("---"):
    23→        return {"name": "", "description": "", "content": text}
    24→    try:
    25→        end = text.index("---", 3)
    26→    except ValueError:
    27→        return {"name": "", "description": "", "content": text}
    28→    frontmatter = text[3:end].strip()
    29→    body = text[end + 3:].strip()
    30→    meta: dict[str, str] = {}
    31→    metadata: dict[str, str] = {}
    32→    current_section: str | None = None
    33→    for line in frontmatter.splitlines():
    34→        if line.startswith("  ") and current_section == "metadata" and ":" in line:
    35→            key, _, val = line.strip().partition(":")
    36→            metadata[key.strip()] = val.strip()
    37→        elif ":" in line:
    38→            key, _, val = line.partition(":")
    39→            k, v = key.strip(), val.strip()
    40→            if not v and k == "metadata":
    41→                current_section = "metadata"
    42→            else:
    43→                current_section = None
    44→                meta[k] = v
    45→    result: dict = {"name": meta.get("name", ""), "description": meta.get("description", ""), "content": body}
    46→    if metadata.get("builtin", "").lower() == "true":
    47→        result["builtin"] = True
    48→    if meta.get("disabled", "").lower() == "true":
    49→        result["disabled"] = True
    50→    return result
    51→
    52→
    53→def _write_skill_md(path: str, name: str, description: str, content: str,
    54→                    *, builtin: bool = False, disabled: bool = False) -> None:
    55→    """Write a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter."""
    56→    lines = [f"name: {name}", f"description: {description}"]
    57→    if disabled:
    58→        lines.append("disabled: true")
    59→    if builtin:
    60→        lines.append("metadata:")
    61→        lines.append("  builtin: true")
    62→    text = "---\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n---\n\n" + content + "\n"
    63→    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    64→    with open(path, "w") as f:
    65→        f.write(text)
    66→
    67→
    68→def list_skills(skills_dir: str) -> list[dict]:
    69→    """List all skills (name + description only).
    70→
    71→    Ordering: built-in skills first, then by directory creation time
    72→    (chronological).
    73→    """
    74→    if not os.path.isdir(skills_dir):
    75→        return []
    76→    result = []
    77→    for entry in os.listdir(skills_dir):
    78→        entry_dir = os.path.join(skills_dir, entry)
    79→        skill_path = os.path.join(entry_dir, "SKILL.md")
    80→        if os.path.isdir(entry_dir) and os.path.isfile(skill_path):
    81→            with open(skill_path) as f:
    82→                parsed = _parse_skill_md(f.read())
    83→            item: dict = {"name": parsed["name"] or entry, "description": parsed["description"]}
    84→            if parsed.get("builtin"):
    85→                item["builtin"] = True
    86→            if parsed.get("disabled"):
    87→                item["disabled"] = True
    88→            # Attach creation time for sorting (not included in response)
    89→            stat = os.stat(entry_dir)
    90→            item["_ctime"] = getattr(stat, "st_birthtime", stat.st_mtime)
    91→            result.append(item)
    92→    # Built-in skills first, then chronological order
    93→    result.sort(key=lambda s: (not s.get("builtin", False), s["_ctime"]))
    94→    for item in result:
    95→        del item["_ctime"]
    96→    return result
    97→
    98→
    99→def get_skill(name: str, skills_dir: str) -> dict | None:
   100→    """Get a single skill with full content. Returns None if not found."""
   101→    skill_path = os.path.join(skills_dir, name, "SKILL.md")
   102→    if not os.path.isfile(skill_path):
   103→        return None
   104→    with open(skill_path) as f:
   105→        return _parse_skill_md(f.read())
   106→
   107→
   108→def create_skill(name: str, description: str, content: str, skills_dir: str) -> None:
   109→    """Create a new skill. Raises SkillValidationError on invalid input or duplicate."""
   110→    _validate_name(name)
   111→    skill_dir = os.path.join(skills_dir, name)
   112→    if os.path.isdir(skill_dir):
   113→        raise SkillValidationError(f"Skill \"{name}\" already exists.")
   114→    _write_skill_md(os.path.join(skill_dir, "SKILL.md"), name, description, content)
   115→
   116→
   117→def update_skill(name: str, description: str, content: str, skills_dir: str) -> None:
   118→    """Update an existing skill. Raises SkillValidationError if not found."""
   119→    skill_path = os.path.join(skills_dir, name, "SKILL.md")
   120→    if not os.path.isfile(skill_path):
   121→        raise SkillValidationError(f"Skill \"{name}\" not found.")
   122→    _write_skill_md(skill_path, name, description, content)
   123→
   124→
   125→def delete_skill(name: str, skills_dir: str) -> None:
   126→    """Delete a skill directory. Raises SkillValidationError if not found or built-in."""
   127→    skill_dir = os.path.join(skills_dir, name)
   128→    if not os.path.isdir(skill_dir):
   129→        raise SkillValidationError(f"Skill \"{name}\" not found.")
   130→    skill_path = os.path.join(skill_dir, "SKILL.md")
   131→    if os.path.isfile(skill_path):
   132→        with open(skill_path) as f:
   133→            parsed = _parse_skill_md(f.read())
   134→        if parsed.get("builtin"):
   135→            raise SkillValidationError(f"Cannot delete built-in skill \"{name}\".")
   136→    shutil.rmtree(skill_dir)
   137→
   138→
   139→def toggle_skill_disabled(name: str, disabled: bool, skills_dir: str) -> dict:
   140→    """Toggle the disabled state of a skill. Returns the updated skill dict."""
   141→    skill_path = os.path.join(skills_dir, name, "SKILL.md")
   142→    if not os.path.isfile(skill_path):
   143→        raise SkillValidationError(f"Skill \"{name}\" not found.")
   144→    with open(skill_path) as f:
   145→        parsed = _parse_skill_md(f.read())
   146→    _write_skill_md(
   147→        skill_path,
   148→        parsed["name"] or name,
   149→        parsed["description"],
   150→        parsed["content"],
   151→        builtin=parsed.get("builtin", False),
   152→        disabled=disabled,
   153→    )
   154→    with open(skill_path) as f:
   155→        return _parse_skill_md(f.read())

1→import os
     2→import threading
     3→
     4→from app.config import MEMORIES_DIR
     5→
     6→_lock = threading.Lock()
     7→
     8→
     9→def _memory_path(user_id: str = "default") -> str:
    10→    user_dir = os.path.join(MEMORIES_DIR, user_id)
    11→    os.makedirs(user_dir, exist_ok=True)
    12→    return os.path.join(user_dir, "MEMORY.md")
    13→
    14→
    15→_SKELETON = "# Agent Memory\n\n## Preferences\n\n## Facts\n\n## Patterns\n"
    16→
    17→
    18→def read_memories(user_id: str = "default") -> str:
    19→    path = _memory_path(user_id)
    20→    with _lock:
    21→        if not os.path.exists(path):
    22→            return ""
    23→        with open(path, "r") as f:
    24→            return f.read()
    25→
    26→
    27→def save_memory(content: str, category: str = "fact", user_id: str = "default") -> str:
    28→    valid_categories = {"preference", "fact", "pattern"}
    29→    if category not in valid_categories:
    30→        category = "fact"
    31→
    32→    section_headers = {
    33→        "preference": "## Preferences",
    34→        "fact": "## Facts",
    35→        "pattern": "## Patterns",
    36→    }
    37→    section_header = section_headers[category]
    38→    entry = f"- {content}"
    39→
    40→    path = _memory_path(user_id)
    41→    with _lock:
    42→        if os.path.exists(path):
    43→            with open(path, "r") as f:
    44→                text = f.read()
    45→        else:
    46→            text = _SKELETON
    47→
    48→        # Exact line-level duplicate check
    49→        existing_lines = text.split("\n")
    50→        if entry in existing_lines:
    51→            return "Memory already exists."
    52→
    53→        # Find section and append
    54→        if section_header in text:
    55→            section_start = text.index(section_header) + len(section_header)
    56→            next_section = text.find("\n## ", section_start)
    57→            if next_section == -1:
    58→                text = text.rstrip() + f"\n{entry}\n"
    59→            else:
    60→                text = text[:next_section].rstrip() + f"\n{entry}\n" + text[next_section:]
    61→        else:
    62→            text = text.rstrip() + f"\n\n{section_header}\n{entry}\n"
    63→
    64→        with open(path, "w") as f:
    65→            f.write(text)
    66→    return "Memory saved."
    67→
    68→
    69→def forget_memory(content: str, user_id: str = "default") -> str:
    70→    path = _memory_path(user_id)
    71→    entry = f"- {content}"
    72→
    73→    with _lock:
    74→        if not os.path.exists(path):
    75→            return "No memories found."
    76→        with open(path, "r") as f:
    77→            lines = f.readlines()
    78→
    79→        found = False
    80→        new_lines = []
    81→        for line in lines:
    82→            if line.rstrip("\n") == entry and not found:
    83→                found = True
    84→                continue
    85→            new_lines.append(line)
    86→
    87→        if not found:
    88→            return "Memory not found."
    89→
    90→        with open(path, "w") as f:
    91→            f.writelines(new_lines)
    92→    return "Memory forgotten."
    93→

     9→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    11→
    12→@dataclass
    13→class ContainerConfig:
    14→    image: str = "duckdb-agent-sidecar:latest"
    15→    runtime: str = "runsc"
    16→    memory_limit: str = "256m"
    17→    cpu_limit: float = 0.5
    18→    max_lifetime_seconds: int = 3600
    19→    idle_timeout_seconds: int = 300
    20→    network: str = "agent-sandbox"
    21→
    22→
    23→@dataclass
    24→class ContainerInfo:
    25→    container_id: str
    26→    session_id: str
    27→    ip_address: str
    28→    port: int = 3000
    29→    created_at: datetime = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))
    30→    last_activity: datetime = field(default=None)
    31→    _container: object = field(default=None, repr=False)
    32→
    33→    host_port: int | None = None
    34→
    35→    def __post_init__(self):
    36→        if self.last_activity is None:
    37→            self.last_activity = self.created_at
    38→
    39→    @property
    40→    def url(self) -> str:
    41→        # Use the published host port only when running natively on macOS.
    42→        # On macOS, Docker containers are in a VM and their bridge IPs are
    43→        # not routable from the host, so we must go via the published port.
    44→        # When the backend itself runs inside a container (docker-compose) or
    45→        # on Linux, both containers share the same network and the direct
    46→        # container IP is reachable — 127.0.0.1 would point at the backend
    47→        # container itself, not the host.
    48→        _on_macos_host = sys.platform == "darwin" and not os.path.exists("/.dockerenv")
    49→        if self.host_port and _on_macos_host:
    50→            return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.host_port}"
    51→        return f"http://{self.ip_address}:{self.port}"
    52→
    53→
    54→class ContainerManager:
    55→    """Manages per-session gVisor-sandboxed sidecar containers."""
    56→
    57→    def __init__(self, config: ContainerConfig | None = None):
    58→        self._config = config or ContainerConfig()
    59→        self._client = docker.from_env()
    60→        self._containers: dict[str, ContainerInfo] = {}
    61→
    62→    def _resolve_network_hosts(self) -> dict[str, str]:
    63→        """Resolve container hostnames to IPs on the sidecar network.
    64→
    65→        gVisor's netstack doesn't use Docker's embedded DNS (127.0.0.11),
    66→        so DNS resolution fails inside runsc containers. We build an
    67→        extra_hosts mapping from container names to their IPs on the
    68→        shared network so /etc/hosts provides the resolution instead.
    69→        """
    70→        hosts: dict[str, str] = {}
    71→        try:
    72→            network = self._client.networks.get(self._config.network)
    73→            network.reload()
    74→            containers = network.attrs.get("Containers", {})
    75→            for _cid, info in containers.items():
    76→                name = info.get("Name", "")
    77→                ipv4 = info.get("IPv4Address", "")
    78→                if name and ipv4:
    79→                    # Strip CIDR suffix (e.g. "172.20.0.2/16" -> "172.20.0.2")
    80→                    ip = ipv4.split("/")[0]
    81→                    hosts[name] = ip
    82→        except Exception as e:
    83→            logger.warning("Failed to resolve network hosts: %s", e)
    84→        return hosts
    85→
    86→    def _resolve_host_gateway_ip(self) -> str | None:
    87→        """Get the host IP reachable from sidecar containers.
    88→
    89→        Docker's "host-gateway" magic value resolves to the docker0 bridge IP,
    90→        not to the gateway of our custom network. Under gVisor the value may
    91→        also not be honoured at all. Instead we read the gateway IP directly
    92→        from the sidecar network's IPAM config — this is the host-side bridge
    93→        address that containers on that network can actually route to.
    94→        """
    95→        try:
    96→            network = self._client.networks.get(self._config.network)
    97→            network.reload()
    98→            for cfg in network.attrs.get("IPAM", {}).get("Config", []):
    99→                gateway = cfg.get("Gateway")
   100→                if gateway:
   101→                    logger.info("Resolved host.docker.internal gateway to %s", gateway)
   102→                    return gateway
   103→        except Exception as e:
   104→            logger.warning("Failed to resolve host gateway IP: %s", e)
   105→        return None
   106→
   107→    def create(self, session_id: str, env: dict[str, str]) -> ContainerInfo:
   108→        """Spin up a new sidecar container for a session."""
   109→        if session_id in self._containers:
   110→            return self._containers[session_id]
   111→
   112→        # Skills volume: mount the host skills directory into the sidecar
   113→        # so it can discover dynamically created skills.
   114→        skills_host_path = os.environ.get("SKILLS_HOST_PATH", "")
   115→        if not skills_host_path:
   116→            # When running natively on the host (not inside Docker),
   117→            # compute the skills directory from this file's location.
   118→            # container_manager.py is at backend/app/, skills/ is at project root.
   119→            if not os.path.exists("/.dockerenv"):
   120→                fallback = os.path.abspath(
   121→                    os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "..", "skills")
   122→                )
   123→                if os.path.isdir(fallback):
   124→                    skills_host_path = fallback
   125→        # Plugins volume: mount the host plugins directory into the sidecar
   126→        # so the SDK can discover locally installed plugins.
   127→        plugins_host_path = os.environ.get("PLUGINS_HOST_PATH", "")
   128→        if not plugins_host_path:
   129→            if not os.path.exists("/.dockerenv"):
   130→                fallback_plugins = os.path.abspath(
   131→                    os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "..", "plugins")
   132→                )
   133→                if os.path.isdir(fallback_plugins):
   134→                    plugins_host_path = fallback_plugins
   135→
   136→        volumes = {}
   137→        if skills_host_path:
   138→            abs_skills_path = os.path.abspath(skills_host_path)
   139→            volumes[abs_skills_path] = {"bind": "/app/.claude/skills", "mode": "ro"}
   140→        if plugins_host_path:
   141→            abs_plugins_path = os.path.abspath(plugins_host_path)
   142→            volumes[abs_plugins_path] = {"bind": "/app/plugins", "mode": "ro"}
   143→
   144→        # Resolve container hostnames to IPs for gVisor DNS compatibility
   145→        extra_hosts = self._resolve_network_hosts()
   146→        # Resolve host.docker.internal so the sidecar can reach the host.
   147→        # Strategy depends on platform and runtime:
   148→        #
   149→        # - macOS Docker Desktop (any runtime): "host-gateway" works correctly
   150→        #   and resolves to the Mac host.  The IPAM gateway IP points to the
   151→        #   bridge gateway *inside* the Linux VM, which is NOT the Mac host,
   152→        #   so we must NOT use it here.
   153→        #
   154→        # - Linux + runc: "host-gateway" resolves to the docker0 bridge IP
   155→        #   which is routable from the container.
   156→        #
   157→        # - Linux + runsc (gVisor): "host-gateway" may not be honoured.
   158→        #   Read the actual gateway IP from the network's IPAM config instead.
   159→        _on_macos_host = sys.platform == "darwin" and not os.path.exists("/.dockerenv")
   160→        _using_gvisor = self._config.runtime == "runsc"
   161→
   162→        if _using_gvisor and not _on_macos_host:

   166→            else:
   167→                extra_hosts["host.docker.internal"] = "host-gateway"
   168→                logger.warning(
   169→                    "Could not resolve host gateway IP from IPAM; falling back to "
   170→                    "host-gateway magic value (may not work under gVisor on Linux)"
   171→                )
   172→        else:
   173→            extra_hosts["host.docker.internal"] = "host-gateway"
   174→        if extra_hosts:
   175→            logger.info("Sidecar extra_hosts: %s", extra_hosts)
   176→
   177→        container = self._client.containers.run(
   178→            image=self._config.image,
   179→            detach=True,
   180→            runtime=self._config.runtime,
   181→            mem_limit=self._config.memory_limit,
   182→            nano_cpus=int(self._config.cpu_limit * 1e9),
   183→            read_only=True,
   184→            cap_drop=["ALL"],
   185→            security_opt=["no-new-privileges"],
   186→            tmpfs={
   187→                "/tmp": "size=50m",
   188→                "/home/appuser": "size=50m,uid=1000,gid=1000",
   189→                # Separate tmpfs for .claude so it stays owned by appuser
   190→                # and writable for CLI session data, debug logs, etc.
   191→                "/home/appuser/.claude": "size=10m,uid=1000,gid=1000",
   192→            },
   193→            **({"volumes": volumes} if volumes else {}),
   194→            network=self._config.network,
   195→            environment=env,
   196→            extra_hosts=extra_hosts or None,
   197→            # Use public DNS so gVisor's netstack can resolve external hosts
   198→            # (Docker's embedded DNS at 127.0.0.11 doesn't work under runsc)
   199→            dns=["8.8.8.8", "8.8.4.4"],
   200→            # Publish port to a random host port so the host-side backend
   201→            # can reach the sidecar (macOS cannot route to bridge IPs)
   202→            ports={"3000/tcp": None},
   203→            labels={
   204→                "app": "duckdb-agent-sidecar",
   205→                "session_id": session_id,
   206→            },
   207→            auto_remove=False,
   208→        )
   209→
   210→        container.reload()
   211→        networks = container.attrs.get("NetworkSettings", {}).get("Networks", {})
   212→        network_info = networks.get(self._config.network, {})
   213→        ip_address = network_info.get("IPAddress", "127.0.0.1")
   214→
   215→        # Extract the dynamically assigned host port
   216→        port_bindings = container.attrs.get("NetworkSettings", {}).get("Ports", {})
   217→        host_port = None
   218→        tcp_bindings = port_bindings.get("3000/tcp")
   219→        if tcp_bindings and len(tcp_bindings) > 0:
   220→            host_port = int(tcp_bindings[0].get("HostPort", 0)) or None
   221→
   222→        info = ContainerInfo(
   223→            container_id=container.id,
   224→            session_id=session_id,
   225→            ip_address=ip_address,
   226→            host_port=host_port,
   227→            _container=container,
   228→        )
   229→        self._containers[session_id] = info
   230→        logger.info(
   231→            "Created sidecar container %s for session %s at %s",
   232→            container.id[:12],
   233→            session_id,
   234→            info.url,
   235→        )
   236→        return info
   237→
   238→    def get(self, session_id: str) -> ContainerInfo | None:
   239→        """Get container info for a session."""
   240→        return self._containers.get(session_id)
   241→
   242→    def touch(self, session_id: str) -> None:
   243→        """Update last_activity timestamp for a session's container."""
   244→        info = self._containers.get(session_id)
   245→        if info is not None:
   246→            info.last_activity = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   247→
   248→    def stop(self, session_id: str) -> None:
   249→        """Stop and remove the container for a session."""
   250→        info = self._containers.pop(session_id, None)
   251→        if info is None:
   252→            return
   253→
   254→        container = info._container
   255→        try:
   256→            container.stop(timeout=5)
   257→        except Exception as e:
   258→            logger.warning("Failed to stop container %s: %s", info.container_id[:12], e)
   259→        try:
   260→            container.remove(force=True)
   261→        except Exception as e:
   262→            logger.warning("Failed to remove container %s: %s", info.container_id[:12], e)
   263→
   264→        logger.info("Stopped sidecar container %s for session %s", info.container_id[:12], session_id)
   265→
   266→    def cleanup_expired(self) -> int:
   267→        """Remove containers that are idle or have exceeded max lifetime."""
   268→        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   269→        idle_cutoff = now - timedelta(seconds=self._config.idle_timeout_seconds)
   270→        lifetime_cutoff = now - timedelta(seconds=self._config.max_lifetime_seconds)
   271→        expired = [
   272→            sid for sid, info in self._containers.items()
   273→            if info.last_activity < idle_cutoff or info.created_at < lifetime_cutoff
   274→        ]
   275→        for sid in expired:
   276→            logger.info("Container for session %s expired (idle or max lifetime), removing", sid)
   277→            self.stop(sid)
   278→        return len(expired)
   279→
   280→    def shutdown_all(self) -> None:
   281→        """Stop and remove all sidecar containers. Called on backend shutdown.
   282→
   283→        In addition to the in-memory registry, queries Docker for any
   284→        containers with the ``app=duckdb-agent-sidecar`` label so that
   285→        orphaned containers (from a previous crash, SIGKILL, or race
   286→        during creation) are also cleaned up.
   287→        """
   288→        # 1. Snapshot tracked IDs before stopping (stop() pops from the dict).
   289→        tracked_ids = {info.container_id for info in self._containers.values()}
   290→        session_ids = list(self._containers.keys())
   291→        for sid in session_ids:
   292→            self.stop(sid)
   293→        tracked_count = len(session_ids)
   294→
   295→        # 2. Find any remaining sidecar containers via Docker labels.
   296→        orphan_count = self._cleanup_by_label(exclude_ids=tracked_ids)
   297→
   298→        logger.info(
   299→            "Shut down %d tracked + %d orphaned sidecar containers",
   300→            tracked_count,
   301→            orphan_count,
   302→        )
   303→
   304→    def _cleanup_by_label(self, *, exclude_ids: set[str] | None = None) -> int:
   305→        """Stop and remove all Docker containers with the sidecar label.
   306→
   307→        Args:
   308→            exclude_ids: Container IDs to skip (already handled elsewhere).
   309→
   310→        Returns the number of containers cleaned up.
   311→        """
   312→        skip = exclude_ids or set()
   313→        cleaned = 0
   314→        try:
   315→            containers = self._client.containers.list(
   316→                filters={"label": "app=duckdb-agent-sidecar"},
   317→                all=True,
   318→            )
   319→        except Exception as e:
   320→            logger.warning("Failed to list sidecar containers by label: %s", e)
   321→            return 0
   322→
   323→        for container in containers:
   324→            if container.id in skip:
   325→                continue  # already handled
   326→            try:
   327→                container.stop(timeout=5)
   328→            except Exception as e:
   329→                logger.warning("Failed to stop orphaned container %s: %s", container.id[:12], e)
   330→            try:
   331→                container.remove(force=True)
   332→            except Exception as e:
   333→                logger.warning("Failed to remove orphaned container %s: %s", container.id[:12], e)
   334→            logger.info("Cleaned up orphaned sidecar container %s", container.id[:12])
   335→            cleaned += 1
   336→        return cleaned
   337→

   201→    @server.call_tool()
   202→    async def call_tool(
   203→        name: str, arguments: dict
   204→    ) -> list[types.TextContent]:
   205→        if name == "execute_sql":
   206→            sql = arguments.get("sql", "")
   207→            try:
   208→                result = await db.execute_query_async(sql)
   209→                truncated_rows = result["rows"][:MAX_RESULT_ROWS]
   210→                result_json = {
   211→                    "status": "success",
   212→                    "columns": result["columns"],
   213→                    "rows": truncated_rows,
   214→                    "rowCount": result["rowCount"],
   215→                }
   216→                return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps(result_json, default=str))]
   217→            except Exception as e:
   218→                error_json = {"status": "error", "error": str(e)}
   219→                return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps(error_json))]
   220→        elif name == "ask_user_question":
   221→            question_data = {
   222→                "question": arguments.get("question", ""),
   223→                "options": arguments.get("options", []),
   224→                "multi_select": arguments.get("multi_select", False),
   225→            }
   226→            question_id = pending_question_store.create(session_id, question_data)
   227→            answer = await pending_question_store.wait(session_id, question_id, timeout=300.0)
   228→            if answer is None:
   229→                result = {"timeout": True, "message": "User did not respond within the time limit."}
   230→            else:
   231→                result = answer
   232→            return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps(result))]
   233→        elif name == "render_chart":
   234→            library = arguments.get("library", "plotly")
   235→
   236→            if library == "vegalite":
   237→                spec = arguments.get("spec")
   238→                if not isinstance(spec, dict):
   239→                    return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({
   240→                        "status": "error",
   241→                        "error": "spec (Vega-Lite specification object) is required when library is 'vegalite'"
   242→                    }))]
   243→                # Check spec has data
   244→                data_obj = spec.get("data", {})
   245→                data_values = data_obj.get("values", []) if isinstance(data_obj, dict) else []
   246→                if not data_values:
   247→                    return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({
   248→                        "status": "error",
   249→                        "error": "Vega-Lite spec must contain data.values with at least one row."
   250→                    }))]
   251→                return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({
   252→                    "status": "success",
   253→                    "chart_spec": {"library": "vegalite", "spec": spec},
   254→                }))]
   255→            else:
   256→                # Plotly path (existing logic)
   257→                data = arguments.get("data")
   258→                layout = arguments.get("layout", {})
   259→                if not isinstance(data, list):
   260→                    logger.warning("render_chart called with missing data: %s", arguments)
   261→                    return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({"status": "error", "error": "data (array of Plotly traces) is required"}))]
   262→
   263→                _DATA_FIELDS = ("x", "y", "z", "values", "labels", "lat", "lon", "r", "theta",
   264→                                "lowerfence", "q1", "median", "q3", "upperfence")
   265→                has_nonempty_trace = False
   266→                for trace in data:
   267→                    if not isinstance(trace, dict):
   268→                        continue
   269→                    for field in _DATA_FIELDS:
   270→                        val = trace.get(field)
   271→                        if isinstance(val, list) and len(val) > 0:
   272→                            has_nonempty_trace = True
   273→                            break
   274→                    if has_nonempty_trace:
   275→                        break
   276→                if not has_nonempty_trace:
   277→                    logger.warning("render_chart called with all-empty data traces: %s", arguments)
   278→                    return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({
   279→                        "status": "error",
   280→                        "error": "All data traces are empty — no data to chart. "
   281→                                 "Check your SQL query results before calling render_chart."
   282→                    }))]
   283→                return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({
   284→                    "status": "success",
   285→                    "chart_spec": {"library": "plotly", "data": data, "layout": layout},
   286→                }))]
   287→        elif name == "create_skill":
   288→            skill_name = arguments.get("name", "")
   289→            description = arguments.get("description", "")
   290→            content = arguments.get("content", "")
   291→            try:
   292→                _create_skill_file(skill_name, description, content, SKILLS_DIR)
   293→                return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({
   294→                    "success": True,
   295→                    "message": f"Skill '{skill_name}' created successfully. Users can now invoke it with /{skill_name}.",
   296→                }))]
   297→            except SkillValidationError as e:
   298→                return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({
   299→                    "success": False,
   300→                    "error": str(e),
   301→                }))]
   302→        elif name == "save_memory":
   303→            content = arguments.get("content", "")
   304→            category = arguments.get("category", "fact")
   305→            result = save_memory(content, category)
   306→            return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({"status": "success", "message": result}))]
   307→        elif name == "recall_memories":
   308→            query = arguments.get("query", "")
   309→            memories = read_memories()
   310→            if query and memories:
   311→                query_lower = query.lower()
   312→                lines = memories.split("\n")
   313→                result_lines: list[str] = []
   314→                current_header: str | None = None
   315→                section_entries: list[str] = []
   316→                for line in lines:
   317→                    if line.startswith("# "):
   318→                        # Top-level header always included
   319→                        if current_header and section_entries:
   320→                            result_lines.append(current_header)
   321→                            result_lines.append("")
   322→                            result_lines.extend(section_entries)
   323→                            result_lines.append("")
   324→                        current_header = None
   325→                        section_entries = []
   326→                        result_lines.append(line)
   327→                        result_lines.append("")
   328→                    elif line.startswith("## "):
   329→                        # Flush previous section if it had matches
   330→                        if current_header and section_entries:
   331→                            result_lines.append(current_header)
   332→                            result_lines.append("")
   333→                            result_lines.extend(section_entries)
   334→                            result_lines.append("")
   335→                        current_header = line
   336→                        section_entries = []
   337→                    elif line.startswith("- ") and query_lower in line.lower():
   338→                        section_entries.append(line)
   339→                # Flush last section
   340→                if current_header and section_entries:
   341→                    result_lines.append(current_header)
   342→                    result_lines.append("")
   343→                    result_lines.extend(section_entries)
   344→                    result_lines.append("")
   345→                memories = "\n".join(result_lines).strip()
   346→            return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({"status": "success", "memories": memories}))]
   347→        elif name == "forget_memory":
   348→            content = arguments.get("content", "")
   349→            result = forget_memory(content)
   350→            return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps({"status": "success", "message": result}))]
   351→        else:
   352→            raise ValueError(f"Unknown tool: {name}")
   353→
   354→    return server
   355→
   356→
   357→async def handle_sse(request: Request) -> Response:
   358→    """Handle SSE connection. Requires session_id query param."""
   359→    session_id = request.query_params.get("session_id")
   360→    if not session_id:
   361→        return Response("session_id query parameter is required", status_code=400)
   362→
   363→    db = session_manager.get_or_create(session_id)
   364→    server = _create_mcp_server(db, session_id)
   365→
   366→    try:
   367→        async with sse_transport.connect_sse(
   368→            request.scope, request.receive, request._send
   369→        ) as streams:
   370→            await server.run(
   371→                streams[0],
   372→                streams[1],
   373→                server.create_initialization_options(),
   374→            )
   375→    except anyio.ClosedResourceError:
   376→        logger.debug("MCP SSE client disconnected (session %s)", session_id)
   377→    except BaseExceptionGroup as eg:
   378→        # The MCP library uses anyio task groups which wrap errors in
   379→        # ExceptionGroups.  Filter out ClosedResourceError (normal client
   380→        # disconnect) and re-raise anything else.
   381→        _, rest = eg.split(anyio.ClosedResourceError)
   382→        if rest:
   383→            raise rest from None
   384→        logger.debug("MCP SSE client disconnected (session %s)", session_id)
   385→
   386→    return Response()
   387→
   388→
   389→mcp_app = Starlette(
   390→    routes=[
   391→        Route("/sse", endpoint=handle_sse, methods=["GET"]),
   392→        Mount("/messages/", app=sse_transport.handle_post_message),
   393→    ]
   394→)

1→from fastapi import APIRouter

     3→from pydantic import BaseModel

     5→from app.agent_memory import read_memories, forget_memory
     6→
     7→router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["memories"])
     8→
     9→
    10→class DeleteMemoryRequest(BaseModel):
    11→    content: str
    12→
    13→
    14→@router.get("/memories")
    15→async def api_list_memories():
    16→    raw = read_memories(user_id="default")
    17→    entries = []
    18→    current_category = "fact"
    19→    category_map = {
    20→        "## Preferences": "preference",
    21→        "## Facts": "fact",
    22→        "## Patterns": "pattern",
    23→    }
    24→    for line in raw.split("\n"):
    25→        stripped = line.strip()
    26→        if stripped in category_map:
    27→            current_category = category_map[stripped]
    28→        elif stripped.startswith("- "):
    29→            entries.append({
    30→                "category": current_category,
    31→                "content": stripped[2:],
    32→            })
    33→    return {"entries": entries, "raw": raw}
    34→
    35→
    36→@router.delete("/memories")
    37→async def api_delete_memory(request: DeleteMemoryRequest):
    38→    result = forget_memory(request.content, user_id="default")
    39→    if result != "Memory forgotten.":
    40→        return JSONResponse(status_code=404, content={"error": result})
    41→    return {"status": "deleted"}
    42→

**Goal:** Store skills and memories in S3-compatible storage using git-remote-s3, with both backend and sidecar as git clients.

```python
"""S3 STS credential generation for sidecar containers."""

import json
import os

import boto3


def _get_sts_client():
    """Create an STS client using long-lived credentials.

    Returns None if STS is not configured or unavailable.
    """
    endpoint_url = os.getenv("STS_ENDPOINT_URL", "")
    access_key = os.getenv("S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "")
    secret_key = os.getenv("S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "")
    region = os.getenv("S3_REGION", "us-east-1")

    if not endpoint_url or not access_key:
        return None

    try:
        return boto3.client(
            "sts",
            endpoint_url=endpoint_url,
            aws_access_key_id=access_key,
            aws_secret_access_key=secret_key,
            region_name=region,
        )
    except Exception:
        return None


def generate_scoped_token(user_id: str, ttl: int = 1200) -> dict:
    """Generate a short-lived STS token scoped to this user's resources.

    Args:
        user_id: User ID for scoping memory access.
        ttl: Token lifetime in seconds (default 20 min).

    Returns:
        Dict with access_key_id, secret_access_key, session_token, expiration.
    """
    bucket = os.getenv("S3_BUCKET", "agent-data")

    sts_client = _get_sts_client()

    if sts_client is None:
        # Fallback: return long-lived credentials directly
        return {
            "access_key_id": os.getenv("S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", ""),
            "secret_access_key": os.getenv("S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", ""),
            "session_token": "",
            "expiration": "",
        }

    policy = json.dumps(
        {
            "Version": "2012-10-17",
            "Statement": [
                {
                    "Effect": "Allow",
                    "Action": [
                        "s3:GetObject",
                        "s3:PutObject",
                        "s3:DeleteObject",
                        "s3:ListBucket",
                    ],
                    "Resource": [
                        f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}",
                        f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}/skills/*",
                        f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}/memories/{user_id}/*",
                    ],
                }
            ],
        }
    )

    response = sts_client.assume_role(
        RoleArn=f"arn:aws:iam::000000000000:role/sidecar-{user_id}",
        RoleSessionName=f"sidecar-{user_id}",
        Policy=policy,
        DurationSeconds=ttl,
    )

    creds = response["Credentials"]
    return {
        "access_key_id": creds["AccessKeyId"],
        "secret_access_key": creds["SecretAccessKey"],
        "session_token": creds["SessionToken"],
        "expiration": str(creds["Expiration"]),
    }

```python
"""Git repository manager for S3-backed skills and memories."""

import os
import subprocess


class GitRepoManager:
    """Manages local git working directories that sync with S3 via git-remote-s3."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        repos_dir: str = "",
        bucket: str = "",
        endpoint_url: str = "",
        access_key_id: str = "",
        secret_access_key: str = "",
        region: str = "",
    ):
        self.repos_dir = repos_dir or os.getenv(
            "GIT_REPOS_DIR", "/app/git-repos"
        )
        self.bucket = bucket or os.getenv("S3_BUCKET", "agent-data")
        self.endpoint_url = endpoint_url or os.getenv(
            "S3_ENDPOINT_URL", ""
        )
        self.access_key_id = access_key_id or os.getenv(
            "S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", ""
        )
        self.secret_access_key = secret_access_key or os.getenv(
            "S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", ""
        )
        self.region = region or os.getenv("S3_REGION", "us-east-1")

    def _git_env(self) -> dict:
        """Build environment dict for git/git-remote-s3 subprocesses."""
        env = os.environ.copy()
        if self.endpoint_url:
            env["AWS_ENDPOINT_URL"] = self.endpoint_url
        if self.access_key_id:
            env["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] = self.access_key_id
        if self.secret_access_key:
            env["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] = self.secret_access_key
        if self.region:
            env["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"] = self.region
        return env

    def clone_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone a remote S3 repo into repos_dir/local_name.

        Returns the local path.
        Raises CalledProcessError if clone fails.
        """
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", remote_url, local_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=self._git_env(),
        )
        return local_path

    def init_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Initialize a new repo and push to remote (for first-time setup).

        Returns the local path.
        """
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        os.makedirs(local_path, exist_ok=True)
        env = self._git_env()

        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "init"],
            cwd=local_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "commit", "--allow-empty", "-m", "initial commit"],
            cwd=local_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", remote_url],
            cwd=local_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "push", "-u", "origin", "main"],
            cwd=local_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        return local_path

    def clone_or_init(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone the repo, or init+push if the remote is empty."""
        try:
            return self.clone_repo(remote_url, local_name)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return self.init_repo(remote_url, local_name)

    def pull(self, repo_path: str) -> None:
        """Pull latest changes from remote."""
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "pull", "--ff-only"],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=self._git_env(),
        )

    def commit_and_push(self, repo_path: str, message: str) -> None:
        """Stage all changes, commit, rebase-pull, and push."""
        env = self._git_env()
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "add", "-A"],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "commit", "-m", message],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "pull", "--rebase"],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "push"],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )

    def ensure_user_memory_repo(self, user_id: str) -> str:
        """Ensure the per-user memory repo exists locally. Clone or init."""
        local_name = f"memories/{user_id}"
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)

        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(local_path, ".git")):
            return local_path

        remote_url = f"s3://{self.bucket}/memories/{user_id}"
        try:
            return self.clone_repo(remote_url, local_name)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return self.init_repo(remote_url, local_name)

    def skills_repo_path(self) -> str:
        """Return the local path to the skills repo."""
        return os.path.join(self.repos_dir, "skills")

    def memory_repo_path(self, user_id: str) -> str:
        """Return the local path to a user's memory repo."""
        return os.path.join(self.repos_dir, "memories", user_id)

    def init_repos(self) -> None:
        """Clone or init the shared skills repo on startup."""
        skills_remote = f"s3://{self.bucket}/skills"
        self.clone_or_init(skills_remote, "skills")

        # Configure git identity in the skills repo
        skills_path = self.skills_repo_path()
        env = self._git_env()
        for cmd in [
            ["git", "config", "user.name", "duckdb-agent-backend"],
            ["git", "config", "user.email", "backend@duckdb-agent.local"],
        ]:
            subprocess.run(
                cmd, cwd=skills_path, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env
            )

def read_memories_s3(user_id: str, repo_manager) -> str:

    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)

        return ""
    with open(memory_file) as f:
        return f.read()


def forget_memory_s3(content: str, user_id: str, repo_manager) -> bool:
    """Forget a memory entry and push to S3."""
    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
    repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
    try:
        repo_manager.pull(repo_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    result = forget_memory(content, user_id=user_id)
    if result:
        repo_manager.commit_and_push(repo_path, f"forget memory: {content[:50]}")

**Actually, a cleaner approach:** The S3 functions should operate on the git repo path directly, not rely on the global `MEMORIES_DIR`. Refactor `forget_memory` to accept an optional `memories_dir` parameter, or have the S3 functions do their own file I/O.

```python
# --- S3 mode (git-backed) ---


def read_memories_s3(user_id: str, repo_manager) -> str:
    """Read memories from git-backed repo (pulls first)."""
    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
    repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
    try:
        repo_manager.pull(repo_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    memory_file = os.path.join(repo_path, "MEMORY.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(memory_file):
        return ""
    with _lock:
        with open(memory_file) as f:
            return f.read()


def forget_memory_s3(content: str, user_id: str, repo_manager) -> bool:
    """Forget a memory entry and push to S3."""
    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
    repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
    try:
        repo_manager.pull(repo_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    memory_file = os.path.join(repo_path, "MEMORY.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(memory_file):
        return False
    with _lock:
        with open(memory_file) as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
        target = f"- {content}\n"
        if target not in lines:
            return False
        lines.remove(target)
        with open(memory_file, "w") as f:
            f.writelines(lines)
    repo_manager.commit_and_push(repo_path, f"forget memory: {content[:50]}")
    return True
```

**Step 1: Implement migration**

```python
"""One-time migration of local skills/memories to S3-backed git repos."""

import os
import shutil


MIGRATION_MARKER = ".s3_migrated"


def migrate_if_needed(
    local_skills_dir: str,
    local_memories_dir: str,
    repo_manager,
) -> None:
    """Copy existing local files into git repos on first S3 enable."""
    marker = os.path.join(repo_manager.repos_dir, MIGRATION_MARKER)
    if os.path.isfile(marker):
        return

    # Migrate skills
    skills_repo = repo_manager.skills_repo_path()
    if os.path.isdir(local_skills_dir):
        for name in os.listdir(local_skills_dir):
            src = os.path.join(local_skills_dir, name)
            dst = os.path.join(skills_repo, name)
            if os.path.isdir(src) and not os.path.exists(dst):
                shutil.copytree(src, dst)
        try:
            repo_manager.commit_and_push(skills_repo, "migrate: import existing skills")
        except Exception:
            pass  # no changes to commit

    # Migrate memories (per-user dirs)
    if os.path.isdir(local_memories_dir):
        for user_id in os.listdir(local_memories_dir):
            user_mem_src = os.path.join(local_memories_dir, user_id)
            if not os.path.isdir(user_mem_src):
                continue
            repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
            mem_repo = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
            for fname in os.listdir(user_mem_src):
                src = os.path.join(user_mem_src, fname)
                dst = os.path.join(mem_repo, fname)
                if os.path.isfile(src) and not os.path.exists(dst):
                    shutil.copy2(src, dst)
            try:
                repo_manager.commit_and_push(
                    mem_repo, f"migrate: import memories for {user_id}"
                )
            except Exception:
                pass

    # Mark as done
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(marker), exist_ok=True)
    with open(marker, "w") as f:
        f.write("migrated\n")
```

#!/bin/bash
# Clone skills and memories repos from S3 if env vars are set.

        echo "[git-init] Clone failed (empty remote?), initializing"
        mkdir -p "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills"
        cd "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills"
        git init
        git commit --allow-empty -m "initial commit"
        git remote add origin "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE"
    }
fi

# Symlink skills into /app/.claude/skills/ for SDK discovery
rm -rf "$SKILLS_DIR"/*
for skill_dir in "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills"/*/; do
    if [ -f "$skill_dir/SKILL.md" ]; then
        skill_name=$(basename "$skill_dir")
        ln -sf "$skill_dir" "$SKILLS_DIR/$skill_name"

# Clone memories repo
if [ -n "$GIT_MEMORIES_REMOTE" ] && [ ! -d "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories/.git" ]; then

#!/bin/bash
# Push any uncommitted changes in skills and memories repos to S3.
set -e

if [ -z "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE" ]; then
    exit 0
fi

    local repo_name="$2"

        return
    fi

    cd "$repo_path"

    # Check for changes
    if git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet && [ -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
        echo "[git-push] No changes in $repo_name"
        return
    fi

    echo "[git-push] Pushing changes in $repo_name"
    git add -A
    git commit -m "auto-commit: session changes" || true
    git pull --rebase || {
        echo "[git-push] Rebase conflict in $repo_name, resolving with ours"
        git checkout --ours .
        git add -A
        git rebase --continue || git rebase --abort
    }
    git push || echo "[git-push] Push failed for $repo_name"
}

push_repo "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills" "skills"
push_repo "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories" "memories"

# Notify backend
curl -s -X POST "$REDACTED" || true

echo "[git-push] Done"

**Approach:** Create a lightweight local MCP server in the sidecar that provides just the skill/memory tools. The sidecar would connect to two MCP servers: the backend one (for SQL, charts) and a local one (for skills/memories).

Create `sidecar/src/local-tools.ts`:

```typescript
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, existsSync, readdirSync } from "fs";
import { join } from "path";

const GIT_REPOS_DIR = process.env.GIT_REPOS_DIR || "/app/git-repos";

export interface ToolResult {
  content: Array<{ type: string; text: string }>;
  isError?: boolean;
}

export function saveMemory(content: string, category: string): ToolResult {
  const memoryFile = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "memories", "MEMORY.md");
  const validCategories = ["preference", "fact", "pattern"];
  if (!validCategories.includes(category)) {
    return {
      content: [{ type: "text", text: `Invalid category. Use: ${validCategories.join(", ")}` }],
      isError: true,
    };
  }

  const sectionMap: Record<string, string> = {
    preference: "## Preferences",
    fact: "## Facts",
    pattern: "## Patterns",
  };

  let text = "";
  if (existsSync(memoryFile)) {
    text = readFileSync(memoryFile, "utf-8");
  } else {
    mkdirSync(join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "memories"), { recursive: true });
    text = "# Agent Memory\n\n## Preferences\n\n## Facts\n\n## Patterns\n";
  }

  const section = sectionMap[category];
  const entry = `- ${content}\n`;
  if (text.includes(entry)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "Memory already exists." }] };
  }

  const idx = text.indexOf(section);
  if (idx === -1) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Section ${section} not found.` }], isError: true };
  }
  const insertPos = idx + section.length + 1;
  text = text.slice(0, insertPos) + entry + text.slice(insertPos);
  writeFileSync(memoryFile, text);
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Memory saved to ${category}.` }] };
}

export function recallMemories(query?: string): ToolResult {
  const memoryFile = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "memories", "MEMORY.md");
  if (!existsSync(memoryFile)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "No memories found." }] };
  }
  let text = readFileSync(memoryFile, "utf-8");
  if (query) {
    const lines = text.split("\n").filter(
      (l) => l.startsWith("- ") && l.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())
    );
    text = lines.length > 0 ? lines.join("\n") : "No matching memories found.";
  }
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text }] };
}

export function forgetMemory(content: string): ToolResult {
  const memoryFile = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "memories", "MEMORY.md");
  if (!existsSync(memoryFile)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "No memories found." }], isError: true };
  }
  let text = readFileSync(memoryFile, "utf-8");
  const target = `- ${content}\n`;
  if (!text.includes(target)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "Memory not found." }], isError: true };
  }
  text = text.replace(target, "");
  writeFileSync(memoryFile, text);
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "Memory forgotten." }] };
}

export function createSkill(name: string, description: string, content: string): ToolResult {
  const nameRegex = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$/;
  if (!nameRegex.test(name)) {
    return {
      content: [{ type: "text", text: "Invalid name. Use lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, 1-64 chars." }],
      isError: true,
    };
  }
  const skillDir = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "skills", name);
  if (existsSync(skillDir)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Skill '${name}' already exists.` }], isError: true };
  }
  mkdirSync(skillDir, { recursive: true });
  const md = `---\nname: ${name}\ndescription: ${description}\n---\n${content}`;
  writeFileSync(join(skillDir, "SKILL.md"), md);

  // Symlink into .claude/skills for SDK discovery
  const symlinkPath = join(process.cwd(), ".claude", "skills", name);
  try {
    const { symlinkSync } = require("fs");
    symlinkSync(skillDir, symlinkPath);
  } catch {
    // symlink may fail in read-only filesystem, non-critical
  }

  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Skill '${name}' created.` }] };
}

export function updateSkill(name: string, description: string, content: string): ToolResult {
  const skillFile = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "skills", name, "SKILL.md");
  if (!existsSync(skillFile)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Skill '${name}' not found.` }], isError: true };
  }
  const md = `---\nname: ${name}\ndescription: ${description}\n---\n${content}`;
  writeFileSync(skillFile, md);
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Skill '${name}' updated.` }] };
}

push_repo() {
    local repo_path="$1"
    local repo_name="$2"

    git add -A

    if ! git pull --rebase 2>/tmp/git-pull-error.txt; then
        # Check if it's a conflict

            # Write conflict info to a known path for the agent to read

            done
            # Abort rebase for now — let the agent handle it

            exit 1
        fi
    fi

    git push || echo "[git-push] Push failed for $repo_name"
}

```python
"""S3 STS credential generation for sidecar containers."""

import json
import os

import boto3


def _get_sts_client():
    """Create an STS client using long-lived credentials.

    Returns None if STS is not configured or unavailable.
    """
    endpoint_url = os.getenv("STS_ENDPOINT_URL", "")
    access_key = os.getenv("S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "")
    secret_key = os.getenv("S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "")
    region = os.getenv("S3_REGION", "us-east-1")

    if not endpoint_url or not access_key:
        return None

    try:
        return boto3.client(
            "sts",
            endpoint_url=endpoint_url,
            aws_access_key_id=access_key,
            aws_secret_access_key=secret_key,
            region_name=region,
        )
    except Exception:
        return None


def generate_scoped_token(user_id: str, ttl: int = 1200) -> dict:
    """Generate a short-lived STS token scoped to this user's resources.

    Args:
        user_id: User ID for scoping memory access.
        ttl: Token lifetime in seconds (default 20 min).

    Returns:
        Dict with access_key_id, secret_access_key, session_token, expiration.
    """
    bucket = os.getenv("S3_BUCKET", "agent-data")

    sts_client = _get_sts_client()

    if sts_client is None:
        # Fallback: return long-lived credentials directly
        return {
            "access_key_id": os.getenv("S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", ""),
            "secret_access_key": os.getenv("S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", ""),
            "session_token": "",
            "expiration": "",
        }

    policy = json.dumps(
        {
            "Version": "2012-10-17",
            "Statement": [
                {
                    "Effect": "Allow",
                    "Action": [
                        "s3:GetObject",
                        "s3:PutObject",
                        "s3:DeleteObject",
                        "s3:ListBucket",
                    ],
                    "Resource": [
                        f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}",
                        f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}/skills/*",
                        f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}/memories/{user_id}/*",
                    ],
                }
            ],
        }
    )

    response = sts_client.assume_role(
        RoleArn=f"arn:aws:iam::000000000000:role/sidecar-{user_id}",
        RoleSessionName=f"sidecar-{user_id}",
        Policy=policy,
        DurationSeconds=ttl,
    )

    creds = response["Credentials"]
    return {
        "access_key_id": creds["AccessKeyId"],
        "secret_access_key": creds["SecretAccessKey"],
        "session_token": creds["SessionToken"],
        "expiration": str(creds["Expiration"]),
    }
```

**Files:**

**Step 1: Implement the module**

```python
"""Git repository manager for S3-backed skills and memories."""

import os
import subprocess


class GitRepoManager:
    """Manages local git working directories that sync with S3 via git-remote-s3."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        repos_dir: str = "",
        bucket: str = "",
        endpoint_url: str = "",
        access_key_id: str = "",
        secret_access_key: str = "",
        region: str = "",
    ):
        self.repos_dir = repos_dir or os.getenv(
            "GIT_REPOS_DIR", "/app/git-repos"
        )
        self.bucket = bucket or os.getenv("S3_BUCKET", "agent-data")
        self.endpoint_url = endpoint_url or os.getenv(
            "S3_ENDPOINT_URL", ""
        )
        self.access_key_id = access_key_id or os.getenv(
            "S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", ""
        )
        self.secret_access_key = secret_access_key or os.getenv(
            "S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", ""
        )
        self.region = region or os.getenv("S3_REGION", "us-east-1")

    def _git_env(self) -> dict:
        """Build environment dict for git/git-remote-s3 subprocesses."""
        env = os.environ.copy()
        if self.endpoint_url:
            env["AWS_ENDPOINT_URL"] = self.endpoint_url
        if self.access_key_id:
            env["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] = self.access_key_id
        if self.secret_access_key:
            env["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] = self.secret_access_key
        if self.region:
            env["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"] = self.region
        return env

    def clone_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone a remote S3 repo into repos_dir/local_name.

        Returns the local path.
        Raises CalledProcessError if clone fails.
        """
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", remote_url, local_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=self._git_env(),
        )
        return local_path

    def init_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Initialize a new repo and push to remote (for first-time setup).

        Returns the local path.
        """
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        os.makedirs(local_path, exist_ok=True)
        env = self._git_env()

        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "init"],
            cwd=local_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "commit", "--allow-empty", "-m", "initial commit"],
            cwd=local_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", remote_url],
            cwd=local_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "push", "-u", "origin", "main"],
            cwd=local_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        return local_path

    def clone_or_init(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone the repo, or init+push if the remote is empty."""
        try:
            return self.clone_repo(remote_url, local_name)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return self.init_repo(remote_url, local_name)

    def pull(self, repo_path: str) -> None:
        """Pull latest changes from remote."""
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "pull", "--ff-only"],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=self._git_env(),
        )

    def commit_and_push(self, repo_path: str, message: str) -> None:
        """Stage all changes, commit, rebase-pull, and push."""
        env = self._git_env()
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "add", "-A"],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "commit", "-m", message],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "pull", "--rebase"],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "push"],
            cwd=repo_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )

    def ensure_user_memory_repo(self, user_id: str) -> str:
        """Ensure the per-user memory repo exists locally. Clone or init."""
        local_name = f"memories/{user_id}"
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)

        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(local_path, ".git")):
            return local_path

        remote_url = f"s3://{self.bucket}/memories/{user_id}"
        try:
            return self.clone_repo(remote_url, local_name)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return self.init_repo(remote_url, local_name)

    def skills_repo_path(self) -> str:
        """Return the local path to the skills repo."""
        return os.path.join(self.repos_dir, "skills")

    def memory_repo_path(self, user_id: str) -> str:
        """Return the local path to a user's memory repo."""
        return os.path.join(self.repos_dir, "memories", user_id)

    def init_repos(self) -> None:
        """Clone or init the shared skills repo on startup."""
        skills_remote = f"s3://{self.bucket}/skills"
        self.clone_or_init(skills_remote, "skills")

        # Configure git identity in the skills repo
        skills_path = self.skills_repo_path()
        env = self._git_env()
        for cmd in [
            ["git", "config", "user.name", "duckdb-agent-backend"],
            ["git", "config", "user.email", "backend@duckdb-agent.local"],
        ]:
            subprocess.run(
                cmd, cwd=skills_path, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env
            )

# --- S3 mode (git-backed) ---


def read_memories_s3(user_id: str, repo_manager) -> str:
    """Read memories from git-backed repo (pulls first)."""
    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
    repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
    try:
        repo_manager.pull(repo_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    memory_file = os.path.join(repo_path, "MEMORY.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(memory_file):
        return ""
    with _lock:
        with open(memory_file) as f:
            return f.read()


def forget_memory_s3(content: str, user_id: str, repo_manager) -> bool:
    """Forget a memory entry and push to S3."""
    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
    repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
    try:
        repo_manager.pull(repo_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    memory_file = os.path.join(repo_path, "MEMORY.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(memory_file):
        return False
    with _lock:
        with open(memory_file) as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
        target = f"- {content}\n"
        if target not in lines:
            return False
        lines.remove(target)
        with open(memory_file, "w") as f:
            f.writelines(lines)
    repo_manager.commit_and_push(repo_path, f"forget memory: {content[:50]}")
    return True

### Task 17: Add migration logic

**Step 1: Implement migration**

```python
"""One-time migration of local skills/memories to S3-backed git repos."""

import os
import shutil


MIGRATION_MARKER = ".s3_migrated"


def migrate_if_needed(
    local_skills_dir: str,
    local_memories_dir: str,
    repo_manager,
) -> None:
    """Copy existing local files into git repos on first S3 enable."""
    marker = os.path.join(repo_manager.repos_dir, MIGRATION_MARKER)
    if os.path.isfile(marker):
        return

    # Migrate skills
    skills_repo = repo_manager.skills_repo_path()
    if os.path.isdir(local_skills_dir):
        for name in os.listdir(local_skills_dir):
            src = os.path.join(local_skills_dir, name)
            dst = os.path.join(skills_repo, name)
            if os.path.isdir(src) and not os.path.exists(dst):
                shutil.copytree(src, dst)
        try:
            repo_manager.commit_and_push(skills_repo, "migrate: import existing skills")
        except Exception:
            pass  # no changes to commit

    # Migrate memories (per-user dirs)
    if os.path.isdir(local_memories_dir):
        for user_id in os.listdir(local_memories_dir):
            user_mem_src = os.path.join(local_memories_dir, user_id)
            if not os.path.isdir(user_mem_src):
                continue
            repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
            mem_repo = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
            for fname in os.listdir(user_mem_src):
                src = os.path.join(user_mem_src, fname)
                dst = os.path.join(mem_repo, fname)
                if os.path.isfile(src) and not os.path.exists(dst):
                    shutil.copy2(src, dst)
            try:
                repo_manager.commit_and_push(
                    mem_repo, f"migrate: import memories for {user_id}"
                )
            except Exception:
                pass

    # Mark as done
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(marker), exist_ok=True)
    with open(marker, "w") as f:
        f.write("migrated\n")
```

#!/bin/bash
# Push any uncommitted changes in skills and memories repos to S3.
set -e

if [ -z "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE" ]; then
    exit 0
fi

GIT_REPOS_DIR="${GIT_REPOS_DIR:-/app/git-repos}"

push_repo() {
    local repo_path="$1"
    local repo_name="$2"

    if [ ! -d "$repo_path/.git" ]; then
        return
    fi

    cd "$repo_path"

    # Check for changes
    if git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet && [ -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
        echo "[git-push] No changes in $repo_name"
        return
    fi

    echo "[git-push] Pushing changes in $repo_name"
    git add -A
    git commit -m "auto-commit: session changes" || true
    git pull --rebase || {
        echo "[git-push] Rebase conflict in $repo_name, resolving with ours"
        git checkout --ours .
        git add -A
        git rebase --continue || git rebase --abort
    }
    git push || echo "[git-push] Push failed for $repo_name"
}

push_repo "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills" "skills"
push_repo "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories" "memories"

# Notify backend
curl -s -X POST "$REDACTED" || true

echo "[git-push] Done"

However, looking at the current architecture, the sidecar passes tools to the SDK via the MCP server connection. Since we're removing these tools from the MCP server, we need a different approach.

**Approach:** Create a lightweight local MCP server in the sidecar that provides just the skill/memory tools. The sidecar would connect to two MCP servers: the backend one (for SQL, charts) and a local one (for skills/memories).

Create `sidecar/src/local-tools.ts`:

```typescript
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, existsSync, readdirSync } from "fs";
import { join } from "path";

const GIT_REPOS_DIR = process.env.GIT_REPOS_DIR || "/app/git-repos";

export interface ToolResult {
  content: Array<{ type: string; text: string }>;
  isError?: boolean;
}

export function saveMemory(content: string, category: string): ToolResult {
  const memoryFile = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "memories", "MEMORY.md");
  const validCategories = ["preference", "fact", "pattern"];
  if (!validCategories.includes(category)) {
    return {
      content: [{ type: "text", text: `Invalid category. Use: ${validCategories.join(", ")}` }],
      isError: true,
    };
  }

  const sectionMap: Record<string, string> = {
    preference: "## Preferences",
    fact: "## Facts",
    pattern: "## Patterns",
  };

  let text = "";
  if (existsSync(memoryFile)) {
    text = readFileSync(memoryFile, "utf-8");
  } else {
    mkdirSync(join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "memories"), { recursive: true });
    text = "# Agent Memory\n\n## Preferences\n\n## Facts\n\n## Patterns\n";
  }

  const section = sectionMap[category];
  const entry = `- ${content}\n`;
  if (text.includes(entry)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "Memory already exists." }] };
  }

  const idx = text.indexOf(section);
  if (idx === -1) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Section ${section} not found.` }], isError: true };
  }
  const insertPos = idx + section.length + 1;
  text = text.slice(0, insertPos) + entry + text.slice(insertPos);
  writeFileSync(memoryFile, text);
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Memory saved to ${category}.` }] };
}

export function recallMemories(query?: string): ToolResult {
  const memoryFile = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "memories", "MEMORY.md");
  if (!existsSync(memoryFile)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "No memories found." }] };
  }
  let text = readFileSync(memoryFile, "utf-8");
  if (query) {
    const lines = text.split("\n").filter(
      (l) => l.startsWith("- ") && l.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())
    );
    text = lines.length > 0 ? lines.join("\n") : "No matching memories found.";
  }
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text }] };
}

export function forgetMemory(content: string): ToolResult {
  const memoryFile = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "memories", "MEMORY.md");
  if (!existsSync(memoryFile)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "No memories found." }], isError: true };
  }
  let text = readFileSync(memoryFile, "utf-8");
  const target = `- ${content}\n`;
  if (!text.includes(target)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "Memory not found." }], isError: true };
  }
  text = text.replace(target, "");
  writeFileSync(memoryFile, text);
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "Memory forgotten." }] };
}

export function createSkill(name: string, description: string, content: string): ToolResult {
  const nameRegex = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$/;
  if (!nameRegex.test(name)) {
    return {
      content: [{ type: "text", text: "Invalid name. Use lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, 1-64 chars." }],
      isError: true,
    };
  }
  const skillDir = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "skills", name);
  if (existsSync(skillDir)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Skill '${name}' already exists.` }], isError: true };
  }
  mkdirSync(skillDir, { recursive: true });
  const md = `---\nname: ${name}\ndescription: ${description}\n---\n${content}`;
  writeFileSync(join(skillDir, "SKILL.md"), md);

  // Symlink into .claude/skills for SDK discovery
  const symlinkPath = join(process.cwd(), ".claude", "skills", name);
  try {
    const { symlinkSync } = require("fs");
    symlinkSync(skillDir, symlinkPath);
  } catch {
    // symlink may fail in read-only filesystem, non-critical
  }

  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Skill '${name}' created.` }] };
}

export function updateSkill(name: string, description: string, content: string): ToolResult {
  const skillFile = join(GIT_REPOS_DIR, "skills", name, "SKILL.md");
  if (!existsSync(skillFile)) {
    return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Skill '${name}' not found.` }], isError: true };
  }
  const md = `---\nname: ${name}\ndescription: ${description}\n---\n${content}`;
  writeFileSync(skillFile, md);
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Skill '${name}' updated.` }] };
}
```

In the shutdown handler, if `git-push.sh` exits with code 1 and `/tmp/git-conflict.txt` exists, the sidecar should attempt to surface the conflict to the user (if the session is still active) or auto-resolve (if idle timeout).

    } catch (err: any) {

        console.error("[server] Git conflict detected:\n", conflict);
        // If active session, could notify agent. For now, auto-resolve.
        execSync(
          "cd /app/git-repos/skills && git pull -X ours && git push; " +
          "cd /app/git-repos/memories && git pull -X ours && git push",
          { stdio: "inherit", timeout: 15000 }
        );
      } catch {
        console.error("[server] git-push failed and conflict resolution failed");
      }
    }
  }
  process.exit(0);
}
