# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

## When to Use

```dot
digraph when_to_use {
    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

```dot
digraph process {
    rankdir=TB;

    subgraph cluster_per_task {
        label="Per Task";
        "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent asks questions?" [shape=diamond];
        "Answer questions, provide context" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [shape=box];
        "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    }

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [shape=box];
    "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" -> "Implementer subagent asks questions?";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Answer questions, provide context" [label="yes"];
    "Answer questions, provide context" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?";
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?";
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [label="yes"];
    "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" -> "More tasks remain?";
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [label="no"];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
}
```

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan.

[Read plan file once: docs/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant - all requirements met, nothing extra

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Approved.

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]
Implementer:
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ❌ Issues:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]
Implementer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting

[Spec reviewer reviews again]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant now

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Solid. Issues (Important): Magic number (100)

[Implementer fixes]
Implementer: Extracted PROGRESS_INTERVAL constant

[Code reviewer reviews again]
Code reviewer: ✅ Approved

[Mark Task 2 complete]

...

[After all tasks]
[Dispatch final code-reviewer]
Final reviewer: All requirements met, ready to merge

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

# Spec Compliance Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a spec compliance reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Verify implementer built what was requested (nothing more, nothing less)

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Review spec compliance for Task N"
  prompt: |
    You are reviewing whether an implementation matches its specification.

    ## What Was Requested

    [FULL TEXT of task requirements]

    ## What Implementer Claims They Built

    [From implementer's report]

    ## CRITICAL: Do Not Trust the Report

    The implementer finished suspiciously quickly. Their report may be incomplete,
    inaccurate, or optimistic. You MUST verify everything independently.

    **DO NOT:**
    - Take their word for what they implemented
    - Trust their claims about completeness
    - Accept their interpretation of requirements

    **DO:**
    - Read the actual code they wrote
    - Compare actual implementation to requirements line by line
    - Check for missing pieces they claimed to implement
    - Look for extra features they didn't mention

    ## Your Job

    Read the implementation code and verify:

    **Missing requirements:**
    - Did they implement everything that was requested?
    - Are there requirements they skipped or missed?
    - Did they claim something works but didn't actually implement it?

    **Extra/unneeded work:**
    - Did they build things that weren't requested?
    - Did they over-engineer or add unnecessary features?
    - Did they add "nice to haves" that weren't in spec?

    **Misunderstandings:**
    - Did they interpret requirements differently than intended?
    - Did they solve the wrong problem?
    - Did they implement the right feature but wrong way?

    **Verify by reading code, not by trusting report.**

    Report:
    - ✅ Spec compliant (if everything matches after code inspection)
    - ❌ Issues found: [list specifically what's missing or extra, with file:line references]
```

```python
"""Git repository manager for S3-backed skills and memories."""

import os
import subprocess


class GitRepoManager:
    """Manages local git working directories that sync with S3 via git-remote-s3."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        repos_dir: str = "",
        bucket: str = "",
        endpoint_url: str = "",
        access_key_id: str = "",
        secret_access_key: str = "",
        region: str = "",
    ):
        self.repos_dir = repos_dir or os.getenv("GIT_REPOS_DIR", "/app/git-repos")
        self.bucket = bucket or os.getenv("S3_BUCKET", "agent-data")
        self.endpoint_url = endpoint_url or os.getenv("S3_ENDPOINT_URL", "")
        self.access_key_id = access_key_id or os.getenv("S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "")
        self.secret_access_key = secret_access_key or os.getenv("S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "")
        self.region = region or os.getenv("S3_REGION", "us-east-1")

    def _git_env(self) -> dict:
        """Build environment dict for git/git-remote-s3 subprocesses."""
        env = os.environ.copy()
        if self.endpoint_url:
            env["AWS_ENDPOINT_URL"] = self.endpoint_url
        if self.access_key_id:
            env["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] = self.access_key_id
        if self.secret_access_key:
            env["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] = self.secret_access_key
        if self.region:
            env["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"] = self.region
        return env

    def clone_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone a remote S3 repo into repos_dir/local_name. Returns the local path."""
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", remote_url, local_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=self._git_env(),
        )
        return local_path

    def init_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Initialize a new repo and push to remote (for first-time setup)."""
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        os.makedirs(local_path, exist_ok=True)
        env = self._git_env()

        subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "commit", "--allow-empty", "-m", "initial commit"],
            cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", remote_url],
            cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "push", "-u", "origin", "main"],
            cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
        )
        return local_path

    def clone_or_init(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone the repo, or init+push if the remote is empty."""
        try:
            return self.clone_repo(remote_url, local_name)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return self.init_repo(remote_url, local_name)

    def pull(self, repo_path: str) -> None:
        """Pull latest changes from remote."""
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "pull", "--ff-only"],
            cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=self._git_env(),
        )

    def commit_and_push(self, repo_path: str, message: str) -> None:
        """Stage all changes, commit, rebase-pull, and push."""
        env = self._git_env()
        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(["git", "pull", "--rebase"], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(["git", "push"], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)

    def ensure_user_memory_repo(self, user_id: str) -> str:
        """Ensure the per-user memory repo exists locally. Clone or init."""
        local_name = f"memories/{user_id}"
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)

        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(local_path, ".git")):
            return local_path

        remote_url = f"s3://{self.bucket}/memories/{user_id}"
        try:
            return self.clone_repo(remote_url, local_name)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return self.init_repo(remote_url, local_name)

    def skills_repo_path(self) -> str:
        """Return the local path to the skills repo."""
        return os.path.join(self.repos_dir, "skills")

    def memory_repo_path(self, user_id: str) -> str:
        """Return the local path to a user's memory repo."""
        return os.path.join(self.repos_dir, "memories", user_id)

    def init_repos(self) -> None:
        """Clone or init the shared skills repo on startup."""
        skills_remote = f"s3://{self.bucket}/skills"
        self.clone_or_init(skills_remote, "skills")

        skills_path = self.skills_repo_path()
        env = self._git_env()
        for cmd in [
            ["git", "config", "user.name", "duckdb-agent-backend"],
            ["git", "config", "user.email", "backend@duckdb-agent.local"],
        ]:
            subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=skills_path, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
```

class GitRepoManager:
    """Manages local git working directories that sync with S3 via git-remote-s3."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        repos_dir: str = "",
        bucket: str = "",
        endpoint_url: str = "",
        access_key_id: str = "",
        secret_access_key: str = "",
        region: str = "",
    ):

        self.bucket = bucket or os.getenv("S3_BUCKET", "agent-data")
        self.endpoint_url = endpoint_url or os.getenv("S3_ENDPOINT_URL", "")
        self.access_key_id = access_key_id or os.getenv("S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "")
        self.secret_access_key = secret_access_key or os.getenv("S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "")
        self.region = region or os.getenv("S3_REGION", "us-east-1")

    def _git_env(self) -> dict:
        """Build environment dict for git/git-remote-s3 subprocesses."""
        env = os.environ.copy()
        if self.endpoint_url:
            env["AWS_ENDPOINT_URL"] = self.endpoint_url
        if self.access_key_id:
            env["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] = self.access_key_id
        if self.secret_access_key:
            env["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] = self.secret_access_key
        if self.region:
            env["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"] = self.region
        return env

    def clone_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone a remote S3 repo into repos_dir/local_name. Returns the local path."""
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", remote_url, local_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=self._git_env(),
        )
        return local_path

    def init_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Initialize a new repo and push to remote (for first-time setup)."""
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        os.makedirs(local_path, exist_ok=True)
        env = self._git_env()

        subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "commit", "--allow-empty", "-m", "initial commit"],
            cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", remote_url],
            cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "push", "-u", "origin", "main"],
            cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
        )
        return local_path

    def clone_or_init(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone the repo, or init+push if the remote is empty."""
        try:
            return self.clone_repo(remote_url, local_name)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:

        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)

"""Tests for git repo manager."""

import os
import subprocess
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch, call

import pytest


@pytest.fixture
def repos_dir(tmp_path):
    return str(tmp_path / "git-repos")


def test_pull_runs_git_pull(repos_dir):
    """pull() runs git pull in the given repo directory."""
    from app.git_repo_manager import GitRepoManager

    mgr = GitRepoManager(repos_dir=repos_dir)
    repo_path = os.path.join(repos_dir, "skills")
    os.makedirs(repo_path)

    with patch("app.git_repo_manager.subprocess.run") as mock_run:
        mock_run.return_value = subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0)
        mgr.pull(repo_path)

    mock_run.assert_called_once_with(
        ["git", "pull", "--ff-only"],
        cwd=repo_path,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
        env=mgr._git_env(),
    )


def test_commit_and_push(repos_dir):
    """commit_and_push() stages, commits, pulls rebase, pushes."""
    from app.git_repo_manager import GitRepoManager

    mgr = GitRepoManager(repos_dir=repos_dir)
    repo_path = os.path.join(repos_dir, "skills")
    os.makedirs(repo_path)

    with patch("app.git_repo_manager.subprocess.run") as mock_run:
        mock_run.return_value = subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0)
        mgr.commit_and_push(repo_path, "delete skill foo")

    commands = [c[0][0] for c in mock_run.call_args_list]
    assert commands[0] == ["git", "add", "-A"]
    assert commands[1][:3] == ["git", "commit", "-m"]
    assert "delete skill foo" in commands[1][3]
    assert commands[2] == ["git", "pull", "--rebase"]
    assert commands[3] == ["git", "push"]


def test_clone_repo(repos_dir):
    """clone_repo() runs git clone with the remote URL."""
    from app.git_repo_manager import GitRepoManager

    mgr = GitRepoManager(repos_dir=repos_dir)

    with patch("app.git_repo_manager.subprocess.run") as mock_run:
        mock_run.return_value = subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0)
        mgr.clone_repo("s3://bucket/skills", "skills")

    mock_run.assert_called_once_with(
        ["git", "clone", "s3://bucket/skills", os.path.join(repos_dir, "skills")],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
        env=mgr._git_env(),
    )


def test_init_repo_when_remote_empty(repos_dir):
    """init_repo() creates a new git repo and pushes when remote is empty."""
    from app.git_repo_manager import GitRepoManager

    mgr = GitRepoManager(repos_dir=repos_dir)

    with patch("app.git_repo_manager.subprocess.run") as mock_run:
        mock_run.side_effect = [
            subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0),  # git init
            subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0),  # git commit --allow-empty
            subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0),  # git remote add
            subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0),  # git push
        ]
        mgr.init_repo("s3://bucket/skills", "skills")

    commands = [c[0][0] for c in mock_run.call_args_list]
    assert commands[0] == ["git", "init"]
    assert commands[1][:2] == ["git", "commit"]
    assert commands[2][:3] == ["git", "remote", "add"]
    assert commands[3] == ["git", "push", "-u", "origin", "main"]


def test_ensure_user_memory_repo_clones_if_missing(repos_dir):
    """ensure_user_memory_repo() clones the memory repo for a new user."""
    from app.git_repo_manager import GitRepoManager

    mgr = GitRepoManager(repos_dir=repos_dir, bucket="test-bucket")

    with patch.object(mgr, "clone_repo") as mock_clone:
        with patch.object(mgr, "init_repo") as mock_init:
            mock_clone.side_effect = subprocess.CalledProcessError(128, "git")
            mgr.ensure_user_memory_repo("alice")
            mock_init.assert_called_once_with(
                "s3://test-bucket/memories/alice",
                "memories/alice",
            )


def test_ensure_user_memory_repo_skips_if_exists(repos_dir):
    """ensure_user_memory_repo() does nothing if repo dir already exists."""
    from app.git_repo_manager import GitRepoManager

    mgr = GitRepoManager(repos_dir=repos_dir, bucket="test-bucket")
    repo_path = os.path.join(repos_dir, "memories", "alice")
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(repo_path, ".git"))

    with patch.object(mgr, "clone_repo") as mock_clone:
        mgr.ensure_user_memory_repo("alice")
        mock_clone.assert_not_called()

"""S3 STS credential generation for sidecar containers."""

import json
import os

import boto3


def _get_sts_client():
    """Create an STS client using long-lived credentials.

    Returns None if STS is not configured or unavailable.
    """
    endpoint_url = os.getenv("STS_ENDPOINT_URL", "")
    access_key = os.getenv("S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "")
    secret_key = os.getenv("S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "")
    region = os.getenv("S3_REGION", "us-east-1")

    if not endpoint_url or not access_key:
        return None

    try:
        return boto3.client(
            "sts",
            endpoint_url=endpoint_url,
            aws_access_key_id=access_key,
            aws_secret_access_key=secret_key,
            region_name=region,
        )
    except Exception:
        return None


def generate_scoped_token(user_id: str, ttl: int = 1200) -> dict:
    """Generate a short-lived STS token scoped to this user's resources."""
    bucket = os.getenv("S3_BUCKET", "agent-data")

    sts_client = _get_sts_client()

    if sts_client is None:
        return {
            "access_key_id": os.getenv("S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", ""),
            "secret_access_key": os.getenv("S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", ""),
            "session_token": "",
            "expiration": "",
        }

    policy = json.dumps(
        {
            "Version": "2012-10-17",
            "Statement": [
                {
                    "Effect": "Allow",
                    "Action": [
                        "s3:GetObject",
                        "s3:PutObject",
                        "s3:DeleteObject",
                        "s3:ListBucket",
                    ],
                    "Resource": [
                        f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}",
                        f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}/skills/*",
                        f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}/memories/{user_id}/*",
                    ],
                }
            ],
        }
    )

    response = sts_client.assume_role(
        RoleArn=f"arn:aws:iam::000000000000:role/sidecar-{user_id}",
        RoleSessionName=f"sidecar-{user_id}",
        Policy=policy,
        DurationSeconds=ttl,
    )

    creds = response["Credentials"]
    return {
        "access_key_id": creds["AccessKeyId"],
        "secret_access_key": creds["SecretAccessKey"],
        "session_token": creds["SessionToken"],
        "expiration": str(creds["Expiration"]),
    }
```

```python
"""Git repository manager for S3-backed skills and memories."""

import os
import subprocess


class GitRepoManager:
    """Manages local git working directories that sync with S3 via git-remote-s3."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        repos_dir: str = "",
        bucket: str = "",
        endpoint_url: str = "",
        access_key_id: str = "",
        secret_access_key: str = "",
        region: str = "",
    ):
        self.repos_dir = repos_dir or os.getenv("GIT_REPOS_DIR", "/app/git-repos")
        self.bucket = bucket or os.getenv("S3_BUCKET", "agent-data")
        self.endpoint_url = endpoint_url or os.getenv("S3_ENDPOINT_URL", "")
        self.access_key_id = access_key_id or os.getenv("S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "")
        self.secret_access_key = secret_access_key or os.getenv("S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "")
        self.region = region or os.getenv("S3_REGION", "us-east-1")

    def _git_env(self) -> dict:
        """Build environment dict for git/git-remote-s3 subprocesses."""
        env = os.environ.copy()
        if self.endpoint_url:
            env["AWS_ENDPOINT_URL"] = self.endpoint_url
        if self.access_key_id:
            env["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] = self.access_key_id
        if self.secret_access_key:
            env["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] = self.secret_access_key
        if self.region:
            env["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"] = self.region
        return env

    def clone_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone a remote S3 repo into repos_dir/local_name. Returns the local path."""
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", remote_url, local_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=self._git_env(),
        )
        return local_path

    def init_repo(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Initialize a new repo and push to remote (for first-time setup)."""
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)
        os.makedirs(local_path, exist_ok=True)
        env = self._git_env()

        subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "commit", "--allow-empty", "-m", "initial commit"],
            cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", remote_url],
            cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "push", "-u", "origin", "main"],
            cwd=local_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
        )
        return local_path

    def clone_or_init(self, remote_url: str, local_name: str) -> str:
        """Clone the repo, or init+push if the remote is empty."""
        try:
            return self.clone_repo(remote_url, local_name)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return self.init_repo(remote_url, local_name)

    def pull(self, repo_path: str) -> None:
        """Pull latest changes from remote."""
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "pull", "--ff-only"],
            cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=self._git_env(),
        )

    def commit_and_push(self, repo_path: str, message: str) -> None:
        """Stage all changes, commit, rebase-pull, and push."""
        env = self._git_env()
        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(["git", "pull", "--rebase"], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)
        subprocess.run(["git", "push"], cwd=repo_path, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env)

    def ensure_user_memory_repo(self, user_id: str) -> str:
        """Ensure the per-user memory repo exists locally. Clone or init."""
        local_name = f"memories/{user_id}"
        local_path = os.path.join(self.repos_dir, local_name)

        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(local_path, ".git")):
            return local_path

        remote_url = f"s3://{self.bucket}/memories/{user_id}"
        try:
            return self.clone_repo(remote_url, local_name)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return self.init_repo(remote_url, local_name)

    def skills_repo_path(self) -> str:
        """Return the local path to the skills repo."""
        return os.path.join(self.repos_dir, "skills")

    def memory_repo_path(self, user_id: str) -> str:
        """Return the local path to a user's memory repo."""
        return os.path.join(self.repos_dir, "memories", user_id)

    def init_repos(self) -> None:
        """Clone or init the shared skills repo on startup."""
        skills_remote = f"s3://{self.bucket}/skills"
        self.clone_or_init(skills_remote, "skills")

        skills_path = self.skills_repo_path()
        env = self._git_env()
        for cmd in [
            ["git", "config", "user.name", "duckdb-agent-backend"],
            ["git", "config", "user.email", "backend@duckdb-agent.local"],
        ]:
            subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=skills_path, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
```

"""Tests for agent memory module in S3 mode."""

import os
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest


@pytest.fixture
def git_memory_dir(tmp_path):
    """Create a fake git-backed memory directory for user 'alice'."""
    mem_dir = tmp_path / "git-repos" / "memories" / "alice"
    mem_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (mem_dir / "MEMORY.md").write_text(
        "# Agent Memory\n\n## Preferences\n- likes python\n\n## Facts\n\n## Patterns\n"
    )
    return str(tmp_path / "git-repos")


@pytest.fixture
def mock_repo_manager(git_memory_dir):

        git_memory_dir, "memories", "alice"
    )
    mgr.ensure_user_memory_repo.return_value = os.path.join(
        git_memory_dir, "memories", "alice"
    )
    mgr.pull = MagicMock()
    mgr.commit_and_push = MagicMock()
    return mgr


def test_read_memories_s3_pulls_first(mock_repo_manager):
    """In S3 mode, read_memories pulls before reading."""
    from app.agent_memory import read_memories_s3

    result = read_memories_s3("alice", mock_repo_manager)

    mock_repo_manager.pull.assert_called_once()
    assert "likes python" in result

    from app.agent_memory import forget_memory_s3

    result = forget_memory_s3("likes python", "alice", mock_repo_manager)

    assert result is True
    mock_repo_manager.commit_and_push.assert_called_once()

# --- S3 mode (git-backed) ---


def read_memories_s3(user_id: str, repo_manager) -> str:
    """Read memories from git-backed repo (pulls first)."""
    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
    repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
    try:
        repo_manager.pull(repo_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    memory_file = os.path.join(repo_path, "MEMORY.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(memory_file):
        return ""
    with _lock:
        with open(memory_file) as f:
            return f.read()


def forget_memory_s3(content: str, user_id: str, repo_manager) -> bool:
    """Forget a memory entry and push to S3."""
    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
    repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
    try:
        repo_manager.pull(repo_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    memory_file = os.path.join(repo_path, "MEMORY.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(memory_file):
        return False
    with _lock:
        with open(memory_file) as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
        target = f"- {content}\n"
        if target not in lines:
            return False
        lines.remove(target)
        with open(memory_file, "w") as f:
            f.writelines(lines)
    repo_manager.commit_and_push(repo_path, f"forget memory: {content[:50]}")
    return True

    """Container past max_lifetime is removed even if recently active."""

    mock_container.id = "abc123"

    """When S3_ENABLED is True, create() injects STS credentials into the container env."""
    mock_container = MagicMock()
    mock_container.id = "abc123"
    mock_container.attrs = {"NetworkSettings": {"Networks": {"agent-sandbox": {"IPAddress": "172.18.0.2"}}}}
    mock_docker_client.containers.run.return_value = mock_container

    }

# --- S3 mode (git-backed) ---


def read_memories_s3(user_id: str, repo_manager) -> str:
    """Read memories from git-backed repo (pulls first)."""
    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
    repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
    try:
        repo_manager.pull(repo_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    memory_file = os.path.join(repo_path, "MEMORY.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(memory_file):
        return ""
    with _lock:
        with open(memory_file) as f:
            return f.read()


def forget_memory_s3(content: str, user_id: str, repo_manager) -> bool:
    """Forget a memory entry and push to S3."""
    repo_path = repo_manager.memory_repo_path(user_id)
    repo_manager.ensure_user_memory_repo(user_id)
    try:
        repo_manager.pull(repo_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    memory_file = os.path.join(repo_path, "MEMORY.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(memory_file):
        return False
    with _lock:
        with open(memory_file) as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
        target = f"- {content}\n"
        if target not in lines:
            return False
        lines.remove(target)
        with open(memory_file, "w") as f:
            f.writelines(lines)
    repo_manager.commit_and_push(repo_path, f"forget memory: {content[:50]}")
    return True
```

### Create `backend/app/routes/git_sync.py`:

"""Git sync endpoint called by sidecar after push."""

from fastapi import APIRouter

from app.config import S3_ENABLED

router = APIRouter()


@router.post("/api/git/sync-complete")
def sync_complete():
    """Sidecar calls this after pushing to S3. Backend pulls to refresh."""
    if not S3_ENABLED:

#!/bin/bash
# Clone skills and memories repos from S3 if env vars are set.
set -e

if [ -z "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE" ]; then
    echo "[git-init] GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE not set, skipping S3 git setup"
    exit 0
fi

GIT_REPOS_DIR="${GIT_REPOS_DIR:-/app/git-repos}"
SKILLS_DIR="/app/.claude/skills"

# Configure git identity
git config --global user.name "duckdb-agent-sidecar"
git config --global user.email "sidecar@duckdb-agent.local"
# Trust the repos directory (git safe.directory)
git config --global --add safe.directory '*'

# Clone skills repo
if [ ! -d "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills/.git" ]; then
    echo "[git-init] Cloning skills repo from $GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE"
    git clone "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE" "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills" || {
        echo "[git-init] Clone failed (empty remote?), initializing"
        mkdir -p "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills"
        cd "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills"
        git init
        git commit --allow-empty -m "initial commit"
        git remote add origin "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE"
    }
fi

# Symlink skills into /app/.claude/skills/ for SDK discovery
mkdir -p "$SKILLS_DIR"
for skill_dir in "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills"/*/; do
    if [ -f "$skill_dir/SKILL.md" ]; then
        skill_name=$(basename "$skill_dir")
        ln -sf "$skill_dir" "$SKILLS_DIR/$skill_name"
    fi
done

# Clone memories repo
if [ -n "$GIT_MEMORIES_REMOTE" ] && [ ! -d "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories/.git" ]; then
    echo "[git-init] Cloning memories repo from $GIT_MEMORIES_REMOTE"

        cd "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories"
        git init

    }

### Create `sidecar/scripts/git-push.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Push any uncommitted changes in skills and memories repos to S3.
set -e

if [ -z "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE" ]; then
    exit 0
fi

GIT_REPOS_DIR="${GIT_REPOS_DIR:-/app/git-repos}"
BACKEND_URL="${BACKEND_BASE_URL:-http://duckdb-data-agent:10000}"

push_repo() {
    local repo_path="$1"
    local repo_name="$2"

    if [ ! -d "$repo_path/.git" ]; then
        return
    fi

    cd "$repo_path"

    # Check for changes
    if git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet && [ -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
        echo "[git-push] No changes in $repo_name"
        return
    fi

    echo "[git-push] Pushing changes in $repo_name"
    git add -A
    git commit -m "auto-commit: session changes" || true
    git pull --rebase || {
        echo "[git-push] Rebase conflict in $repo_name, detecting..."
        if git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | grep -q .; then
            echo "CONFLICT in $repo_name:" > /tmp/git-conflict.txt
            git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U >> /tmp/git-conflict.txt
            # Auto-resolve with ours strategy
            git checkout --ours .
            git add -A
            git rebase --continue || git rebase --abort
        fi
    }
    git push || echo "[git-push] Push failed for $repo_name"
}

push_repo "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills" "skills"
push_repo "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories" "memories"

# Notify backend
curl -s -X POST "$REDACTED" || true

echo "[git-push] Done"
```

#!/bin/bash
# Clone skills and memories repos from S3 if env vars are set.
set -e

if [ -z "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE" ]; then
    echo "[git-init] GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE not set, skipping S3 git setup"
    exit 0
fi

GIT_REPOS_DIR="${GIT_REPOS_DIR:-/app/git-repos}"
SKILLS_DIR="/app/.claude/skills"

# Configure git identity
git config --global user.name "duckdb-agent-sidecar"
git config --global user.email "sidecar@duckdb-agent.local"
# Trust the repos directory (git safe.directory)
git config --global --add safe.directory '*'

# Clone skills repo
if [ ! -d "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills/.git" ]; then
    echo "[git-init] Cloning skills repo from $GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE"
    git clone "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE" "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills" || {
        echo "[git-init] Clone failed (empty remote?), initializing"
        mkdir -p "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills"
        cd "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills"
        git init
        git commit --allow-empty -m "initial commit"
        git remote add origin "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE"
    }
fi

# Symlink skills into /app/.claude/skills/ for SDK discovery
mkdir -p "$SKILLS_DIR"
for skill_dir in "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills"/*/; do
    if [ -f "$skill_dir/SKILL.md" ]; then
        skill_name=$(basename "$skill_dir")
        ln -sf "$skill_dir" "$SKILLS_DIR/$skill_name"
    fi
done

# Clone memories repo
if [ -n "$GIT_MEMORIES_REMOTE" ] && [ ! -d "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories/.git" ]; then
    echo "[git-init] Cloning memories repo from $GIT_MEMORIES_REMOTE"
    git clone "$GIT_MEMORIES_REMOTE" "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories" || {
        echo "[git-init] Clone failed (empty remote?), initializing"
        mkdir -p "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories"
        cd "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories"
        git init
        git commit --allow-empty -m "initial commit"
        git remote add origin "$GIT_MEMORIES_REMOTE"
    }
fi

echo "[git-init] S3 git setup complete"

#!/bin/bash
# Push any uncommitted changes in skills and memories repos to S3.
set -e

if [ -z "$GIT_SKILLS_REMOTE" ]; then
    exit 0
fi

GIT_REPOS_DIR="${GIT_REPOS_DIR:-/app/git-repos}"
BACKEND_URL="${BACKEND_BASE_URL:-http://duckdb-data-agent:10000}"

push_repo() {
    local repo_path="$1"
    local repo_name="$2"

    if [ ! -d "$repo_path/.git" ]; then
        return
    fi

    cd "$repo_path"

    # Check for changes
    if git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet && [ -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
        echo "[git-push] No changes in $repo_name"
        return
    fi

    echo "[git-push] Pushing changes in $repo_name"
    git add -A
    git commit -m "auto-commit: session changes" || true
    git pull --rebase || {
        echo "[git-push] Rebase conflict in $repo_name, detecting..."
        if git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | grep -q .; then
            echo "CONFLICT in $repo_name:" > /tmp/git-conflict.txt
            git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U >> /tmp/git-conflict.txt
            # Auto-resolve with ours strategy
            git checkout --ours .
            git add -A
            git rebase --continue || git rebase --abort
        fi
    }
    git push || echo "[git-push] Push failed for $repo_name"
}

push_repo "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/skills" "skills"
push_repo "$GIT_REPOS_DIR/memories" "memories"

# Notify backend
curl -s -X POST "$REDACTED" || true

echo "[git-push] Done"

1→FROM python:3.12-slim AS build
     2→
     3→# Install Node.js 20
     4→RUN apt-get update && \
     5→    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates && \
     6→    curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - && \
     7→    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs && \
     8→    apt-get clean && \
     9→    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    10→
    11→# Build the sidecar server (needs devDependencies for tsc)
    12→WORKDIR /app
    13→COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
    14→RUN npm ci
    15→COPY tsconfig.json ./
    16→COPY src/ ./src/
    17→RUN npx tsc
    18→
    19→# Production stage
    20→FROM python:3.12-slim
    21→
    22→# Install Node.js 20 and git
    23→RUN apt-get update && \
    24→    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates git && \
    25→    curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - && \
    26→    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs && \
    27→    apt-get clean && \
    28→    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    29→
    30→# Install git-remote-s3 for S3-backed git repositories
    31→RUN pip install --no-cache-dir git-remote-s3
    32→
    33→WORKDIR /app
    34→
    35→# Copy compiled JS and production dependencies only
    36→COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
    37→RUN npm ci --omit=dev
    38→COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
    39→
    40→# Skills are volume-mounted at runtime at /app/.claude/skills/
    41→# Pre-create the directory so Docker can bind-mount onto it even with
    42→# read_only=True (the directory must exist in the image layer).
    43→RUN mkdir -p /app/.claude/skills
    44→RUN mkdir -p /app/plugins
    45→
    46→# Create non-root user
    47→RUN useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash appuser
    48→
    49→# Pre-create git-repos directory for S3-backed git clones
    50→RUN mkdir -p /app/git-repos && chown appuser:appuser /app/git-repos
    51→
    52→COPY scripts/ /app/scripts/
    53→RUN chmod +x /app/scripts/*.sh
    54→
    55→USER appuser
    56→EXPOSE 3000
    57→
    58→CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]
    59→
